WARNING: this book is NOT addressable by Vulgate chapter and verse numbers, and every locus in it is withheld in the verse-alias table. The translator prints Esther in the Septuagint arrangement, with the Greek additions standing where the Greek puts them instead of gathered into an appendix as the Vulgate gathers them, and in fifteen chapters against the Vulgate's sixteen. Nothing lines up: this edition's 1:1 is the Vulgate's 11:2, its 3:1 is the Vulgate's 1:1, and its 13:9 is part of the king's letter where the Vulgate's 13:9 is Mardochai's prayer, “O Lord, Lord, almighty king”. The 1962 Missal's Esther 13:9-11 and 14:12-13 and the Lectionary's Esther 4:17 therefore refuse here rather than resolving to the wrong words. This is the one book of this version a Vulgate citation cannot reach.

Psalm numbers are the Vulgate and Septuagint numbers the 1962 Missal cites, and the psalm inscription is numbered as verse 1. The psalter has 2535 verses against the Douay-Rheims's 2528 and the Clementine's 2527, the difference being extra verse divisions in Psalms 13, 15, 92, 125 and 135; the chapter numbers, the restarted numbering at Psalm 115 and Psalm 147 all agree with the Clementine in number. Two psalm bounds do not. The Vulgate prints Psalm 115 as verses 10 to 19 and Psalm 147 as verses 12 to 20, keeping the numbering each had before the Hebrew split; this edition restarts both at verse 1, so its Psalm 115 runs 1-10 and its Psalm 147 runs 1-9. A citation of Psalm 115:10, which the Vulgate opens the psalm with, would otherwise resolve here to its tenth verse, which is the Vulgate's 115:19, and it is withheld in the verse-alias table; Psalm 147:12-20 falls past the end of the chapter this edition prints and refuses for want of the verses.
TRAP: the Missal abbreviation “Eccle.” is Ecclesiastes; “Eccli.” is Ecclesiasticus, which is under token Ecclus.
